test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the tenure of a Governor in an Indian state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The tenure of the **Governor** of an **Indian state** is governed by **Article 156** of the **Constitution of India**. According to this article, the **Governor** shall hold office for a term of **5 years** from the date on which they enter their office. *Hence, the statement regarding the 5-year term is correct.*

• The **Governor** holds office during the **pleasure of the President**. This means that the **President of India** has the authority to remove a **Governor** at any time before the completion of the **5-year** term without assigning any specific reason.

• A **Governor** may, by writing under their hand addressed to the **President**, resign from their office at any point during their tenure.

• Notwithstanding the expiration of the **5-year** term, the **Governor** shall continue to hold office until their successor enters upon their office to ensure there is no constitutional vacuum in the state administration.

• The option of **3 years** is incorrect as there is no such provision in the **Constitution** for the **Governor**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

• The option of **6 years** is incorrect because this duration typically applies to members of the **Rajya Sabha** and the **State Legislative Council**, or the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**, but not to the **Governor**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

• The option **Until retirement** is incorrect because the **Constitution** does not prescribe a retirement age for the **Governor**, unlike judges of the **Supreme Court** (**65 years**) or **High Court** (**62 years**). *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Constitutional Position**: **Article 153** mandates that there shall be a **Governor** for each state. However, the **7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956** made it possible to appoint the same person as **Governor** for **two or more states**.

• **Appointment**: The **Governor** is not elected but is appointed by the **President** by warrant under his hand and seal as per **Article 155**. This ensures the **Union Government** maintains a degree of control over state administration.

• **Qualifications**: To be eligible for the post of **Governor** under **Article 157**, a person must be a **citizen of India** and must have completed the age of **35 years**. Additionally, they should not hold any **office of profit** and should not be a member of either **House of Parliament** or a **State Legislature**.

• **Executive Powers**: The **Governor** is the **Constitutional Head** of the state. All executive actions of the **State Government** are formally taken in their name. They appoint the **Chief Minister** and, on the **Chief Minister’s** advice, other ministers.

• **Legislative Powers**: The **Governor** has the power to summon or prorogue the **State Legislature** and dissolve the **State Legislative Assembly**. They also address the first session of the **State Legislature** after each **general election** and at the commencement of the first session of each **year**.

**Important Points__**

• **Judicial Immunity**: Under **Article 361**, the **Governor** enjoys personal immunity from legal liability for their official acts. During their term of office, no criminal proceedings can be instituted against them, and they cannot be arrested or imprisoned.

• **Sarkaria Commission (1983)**: This commission recommended that the **Governor’s** **5-year** term should not be disturbed except for extremely compelling reasons. It suggested that the **Governor** should be an eminent person from outside the state and not intimately connected with local politics.

• **Punchhi Commission (2007)**: This commission on **Centre-State Relations** suggested that the phrase **during the pleasure of the President** should be deleted from the **Constitution** because it leads to the arbitrary removal of **Governors**. It recommended a fixed tenure of **5 years** with a provision for **impeachment** by the **State Legislature**.

• **Discretionary Powers**: Unlike the **President**, the **Governor** has certain **discretionary powers**, such as recommending the imposition of **President’s Rule** (**Article 356**) in the state or reserving certain bills for the consideration of the **President** (**Article 200**).

• **Oath of Office**: The oath of office to the **Governor** is administered by the **Chief Justice** of the concerned **State High Court** or, in their absence, the senior-most judge of that court.

57:T
